questions.question: Which Articles of the Constitution of India provide for a parliamentary form of government at the Centre?
questions.solution: Articles 74 and 75 deal with the parliamentary system at the Centre. Article 74 provides for a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President, while Article 75 deals with the appointment, tenure, and responsibility of the ministers.

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Constitution of India mentions that every Minister and the Attorney-General of India shall have the right to speak in and participate in the proceedings of either House of Parliament?
questions.solution: Article 88 grants Ministers and the Attorney-General the right to speak and participate in the proceedings of either House (or any joint sitting), though they do not have the right to vote in a House of which they are not a member.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution explains that the executive power of every state shall be so exercised as not to impede or prejudice the exercise of the executive power of the Union?
questions.solution: Article 257 deals with the control of the Union over States in certain cases, ensuring that State executive power does not impede the Union's executive power and allowing the Union to give necessary directions to States.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 77 of the Indian Constitution:
1. It empowers the Prime Minister to make rules for the transaction of the business of the Government of India.
2. It provides for the allocation of government business among Ministers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution: Only statement 2 is correct. Under Article 77, it is the President (not the Prime Minister) who makes rules for the more convenient transaction of government business and the allocation of said business among Ministers.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution mentions the organisation of 'Village Panchayats'?
questions.solution: Article 40, a Directive Principle of State Policy, directs the State to organize village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 166 of the Indian Constitution:
1. It provides for the conduct of business of the Government of a State.
2. It empowers the Governor to make rules for the convenient transaction of such business and the allocation among Ministers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Article 166 relates to the conduct of business of a State Government, mirroring Article 77 at the Union level, with the Governor making the rules for business transaction and allocation.

questions.question:
Consider the following provisions of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs):
1. Article 36 defines the term “State” for the purpose of Part IV of the Constitution.
2. Article 37 states that the DPSPs are enforceable by the courts.
3. Article 38 directs the State to secure a social order for the promotion of the welfare of the people.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Article 37 explicitly states that DPSPs are not enforceable by any court, though they are fundamental in the governance of the country.

questions.question: Which article of the Constitution of India lays down that it shall be the duty of the Advocate-General to give advice to the Government of the State upon legal matters?
questions.solution: Article 165 provides for the appointment and duties of the Advocate-General for the State, who acts as the corresponding official to the Attorney-General of India at the state level.

questions.question: Articles 245 to 255 in Part XI of the Indian Constitution deal with the ______.
questions.option_2: financial relations between the Centre and the states
questions.option_3: legislative relations between the Centre and the states
questions.solution: Articles 245 to 255 in Part XI deal with legislative relations between the Union and the States, including the distribution of legislative subjects.

questions.question:
Consider the following Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs):
1. Provision for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief – Article 42
2. Promotion of cottage industries on an individual or co-operative basis in rural areas – Article 43
3. Participation of workers in the management of industries - Article 43A
Which of the above is/are correctly matched?
questions.solution: All three are correctly matched. Article 42 covers humane work conditions/maternity relief, Article 43 covers living wages and cottage industries, and Article 43A (added by the 42nd Amendment) covers workers' participation in management.

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution deals with the Panchayats?
questions.solution: Part IX (Articles 243 to 243O) deals with the Panchayats. It was inserted by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Part V (Articles 52 to 78) of the Indian Constitution:
1. It contains provisions related to the President and Vice-President of India.
2. It defines the powers of the Attorney-General for India.
3. It deals with the Union Executive.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: All statements are correct. Part V, Chapter I (Articles 52-78) deals with the Union Executive, which includes the President, Vice-President, Council of Ministers, and the Attorney-General for India.

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian constitution deals with the parliament and its proceedings?
questions.solution: Articles 79 to 122 in Part V deal with the Parliament of India, covering its organization, composition, duration, officers, procedures, and powers.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about environmental protection in the Indian Constitution:
1. The Directive Principles of State Policy include a provision for protecting and improving the environment and safeguarding forests and wildlife.
2. This provision is contained in Article 48-A of the Constitution.
3. Article 48-A was inserted by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: All statements are correct. Article 48A was added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) as a Directive Principle to protect the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘The State shall, in particular, direct its policy towards securing that the ownership and control of the material resources of the community are so distributed as best to subserve the common good’?
questions.solution: Article 39(b) directs the state to ensure that the ownership and control of material resources are distributed for the common good. Article 39(c) seeks to prevent the concentration of wealth.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding provisions in the Indian Constitution:
1. Articles 168 to 212 in Part VI deal with the State Legislature.
2. Articles 214 to 231 relate to the High Courts in the States.
3. Articles 79 to 122 in Part V are about the Parliament of India.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: All statements are correct. These articles correctly define the boundaries for the State Legislature, High Courts, and the Union Parliament respectively.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions the 'Promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections'?
questions.solution: Article 46 directs the State to promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections, particularly the SCs and STs, and to protect them from social injustice.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 79 of the Constitution states that Parliament consists of the President and two Houses — the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
2. Article 82 deals with the composition of the House of the People.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Only statement 1 is correct.
  • Article 79 correctly describes the three components of Parliament.
  • Article 81 (not 82) deals with the Composition of the House of the People. Article 82 is about the Readjustment after each census.

questions.question: In a situation wherein A (female) and B (male) are working in the same office, same designation, same nature of work but unequal payment, which of the following Articles of the Constitution be applicable?
questions.solution: Article 39(d) mandates 'Equal pay for equal work' for both men and women as a Directive Principle of State Policy.

questions.question: Which Articles of the Constitution deal with citizenship?
questions.solution: Part II of the Indian Constitution, spanning Articles 5 to 11, deals with various aspects of Citizenship at the time of the Constitution's commencement and the Parliament's power to regulate it.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 142 empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any case.
2. Article 141 deals with the ancillary powers of the Supreme Court.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Only statement 1 is correct.
  • Article 142 allows the SC to do 'complete justice'.
  • Article 141 states that the law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts in India. Article 140 (not 141) deals with the ancillary powers.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles in the Constitution of India provides protection to the President and Governors and Rajpramukhs?
questions.solution: Article 361 provides immunity to the President and Governors from being answerable to any court for the exercise and performance of their duties and powers of office.

questions.question: Which Article provides that all minorities have the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice?
questions.solution: Article 30 is a fundamental right that grants all minorities, whether based on religion or language, the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution currently contains 22 scheduled languages.
2. Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali were added to the Eighth Schedule by the 71st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Only statement 1 is correct.
  • Statement 1: There are 22 languages in the Eighth Schedule.
  • Statement 2: Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali were added by the 92nd Amendment (2003). The 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali.

questions.question: Article 15 of the Constitution of India entails:
questions.option_1: equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment
questions.option_2: prohibition of discrimination against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth
questions.solution: Article 15 prohibits discrimination by the State against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. Option (a) is Article 16.
